la:verb:detestor.html:
dē-testor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. a.
In relig. lang.
To curse while calling a deity to witness, i. e. to execrate, abominate (for syn. cf.: abominari, adversari, abhorrere, horrere, devovere, execrari): cum (te) viderunt, tamquam auspicium malum detestantur,: omnibus precibus detestatus Ambiorigem, * ; cf.: caput euntis hostili prece,: dira exsecratio ac furiale carmen detestandae familiae stirpique compositum,: exitum belli civilis, et saep.—
To call to witness, = testor, obtestor: summum Jovem, deosque,. —
To call down upon, denounce while invoking a deity: minas periculaque in caput eorum,: deorum iram in caput infelicis pueri,.—
To hate intensely, detest, abominate, abhor: causam auctoremque cladis,: civilia arma adeo detestari,felt such abhorrence for,: sortem populi Romani,: viam pravam .—
Transf., to avert from one's self by entreaty, to ward off, avert, remove, sc. an evil from one's self or others, = deprecari, to deprecate: ut a me quandam prope justam patriae querimoniam detester ac deprecer,: memoriam consulatus tui a republica,: invidiam,: o di immortales, avertite ac detestamini hoc omen,.—
In judic. lang., to renounce solemnly or under oath: detestatum est testatione denuntiatum,; cf. ib. § 40, and detestatio, II.: Servius Sulpicius in libro de sacris detestandis, etc.,.!*? In a pass. sense, Ap. Mag. p. 307, 24; .—Esp., in the part. perf., detested, abominated: detestata omnia ejusmodi repudianda sunt,: bella matribus detestata,.

la:noun:detrimentum.html:
dētrīmentum, i, n.
detero
,
a rubbing off. *
Lit.: limae tenuantis, Ap. M. 6, p. 175, 25.—
Transf., loss, damage, detriment.
In gen. (class.; cf. for syn.: damnum, jactura, incommodum, dispendium): emolumenta et detrimenta (quae ὠφελήματα et βλάμματα appellant) communia esse voluerunt, ; cf. Müll.; so opp. emolumentum,: nostro incommodo detrimentoque doleamus,: afferre,to occasion, cause,; ; cf.: magna inferre,: importare,: accipere, to suffer, in gen., ; ; esp. to suffer defeat in battle, ; ; et saep.: capere, Planc. ap. ; cf. the foll., and facere,; ; : acceptum sarcire,; ; cf. reconcinnare,fin.: in bonum vertere,fin., et saep.: animae suae detrimentum pati,loss, ruin,: detrimentum sui facere,.—
Esp.
In the well-known formula, by which unlimited power was intrusted to the consuls: videant consules (dent magistratus operam, provideant, etc.), ne quid respublica detrimenti capiat (accipiat),; ; ; ; ; —
In the histt., the loss of a battle, defeat, overthrow (cf. calamitas and incommodum, no. II.), ; ; et saep.

la:noun:detractio.html:
dētractĭo, ōnis, f.
detraho
,
a drawing off, taking away, withdrawal.
In gen. (good prose): alieni, opp. appetitio,: doloris,: loci,departure from,: sanguinis,; ; : illa ipsa (sc. Praxitelia capita) efficiuntur detractione,.—
In partic.
Medic. t. t., a purging: cibi,.—More freq. absol., ; et saep.—In plur., ; ; .—
Rhet. t. t., a taking away, leaving out, ellipsis, ; —
Detraction, slander, evil-speaking, .—Plur., .

la:verb:detracto.gloss: to refuse, decline, reject or evade

la:verb:deterreo.gloss: to frighten off, deter, discourage, prevent, hinder
senses: to frighten off, deter, discourage, prevent, hinder
to avert, keep off; repress, control
la:verb:deterreo.html:
dē-terrĕo, ŭi, ĭtum, 2, v. a.
To frighten from any thing; to deter, discourage from, prevent, hinder (class.).—Constr.
(Aliquem) ab aliqua re: homines adolescentes a dicendi studio,: sanos homines a scribendo,; cf. : te a dimicatione (opp. ad certam laudem adhortor),: eum ab instituto consilio,; cf.: a proposito,: animos a cupiditate,: ferociores annos a licentia, et saep.— Without acc.: a turpi meretricis amore,.—
(Aliquem) de aliqua re: de agro hunc senem,: Stoicos de sententia,: me de statu meo, Brut. ap. —
(Aliquem) ne, quin, quominus: (poetam) maledictis, ne scribat,; ; ; (but different is : deterritum putant, ne discerperetur). —Without acc.: haud ferro deterrere potes, ne me amet,.—With quin: quin loquar haec ... numquam me potes deterrere,; ; fin.—Pass., ; cf.: me homo nemo deterruerit, quin ea sit in his aedibus, i. e. shall make me believe but that, etc., .— With quominus: neque te deterreo, quominus id disputes,; ; —
With aliquem and an inf. (very rarely): nefarias ejus libidines commemorare pudore deterreor,; .—(ε) Aliquem aliqua re (very rarely): silvestres homines caedibus et victu foedo,; cf. .—(ζ) With simple acc.: reliquos magnitudine poenae,: pavidam ense (with repellere),: deterritis tribunis,: Caesar coercendum atque deterrendum Dumnorigem statuebat,: in deterrenda liberalitate, .—(η) Absol.: advorsor sedulo et deterreo,; ; —
In Augustan authors, sometimes with an inanimate object, like defendere, prohibere, etc., to avert, keep off: vim a censoribus,: d. nefas et inhibere bipennem,.

la:verb:detergeo.gloss: to wipe off, wipe away, clean by wiping
senses: to wipe off, wipe away, clean by wiping
to chase away, drive away, remove
la:verb:detergeo.html:
dē-tergĕo, si, sum, 2 (also post-class.:
detergis,: detergunt, id. ap. : detergantur,; Ap. Mag. 59, p. 312, 26; , v. tergeo), v. a.
To wipe off, wipe away (class.).
Lit.: sudorem frontis brachio,; cf.: lacrimas pollice,; cf.: teneros fletus stamine,: araneas,.—Poet.: nubila,i. e. to drive away, remove,; cf. sidera, to drive or chase away, .—
Transf., to cleanse by wiping, to wipe off, wipe clean, to clean out: caput pallio,: labra spongiā,; cf.: se linguā,: frontem unguento,: falces fibrina pelle,: cloacas,; cf. .—Comic: mensam,i. e. to clear, to empty,.—
Trop.
To take away, remove: fastidia,: somnum, Pall. et Cel. 27.—
To cleanse, purge: animum helleboro,; secula foedo victu,.—
In colloq. lang., of money: primo anno LXXX. detersimus,have swept off, got,.—
To strip off, break off; to break to pieces: remos,; : pinnas asseribus falcatis,: palmites,

la:adj:deterior.html:
dētĕrĭor, ius,
adj. comp. (sup. deterrimus, a um) [from an obs. adj. deter, from de, down; hence, lower, inferior, worse], worse, poorer, meaner (freq. and class.—for syn. cf.: malus, injustus, improbus; pravus, nequam, corruptus, perversus; and the compp. pejor, etc.).
Of inanimate things: seges, Enn. ap. : ruina rem non fecit deteriorem, haud scio an jam fructuosiorem,: so, vectigalia, * : muraena carne,: deterior ac decolor aetas,: forma,: mores,: via, et saep.: video meliora proboque, Deteriora sequor,: cuncta aucta in deterius,; ; —Sup.: genus reipublicae ex bono in deterrimum conversum,; so, genus,: finis,: causa belli,: color,: cogitare optima simul et deterrima, et saep.—
Of persons: quo deteriores anteponantur bonis,; opp. melior,; ; opp. optimus,; opp. strenuior,: vidi ego nequam homines, verum te neminem deteriorem, et saep.: peditatu erat deterior,weaker,: infideli deterior,.—Sup.: homo deterrime et impudentissime,; .—dēterius, adv., worse, less: de male Graecis Latine scripta deterius,: nequi deterius huic sit quam quoi pessumest,: valeo, Luccei. ap. : olet herba,: spe nostra si placeant,.

la:verb:deterioro.html:
dētĕrĭōro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
deterior
,
to make worse, to deteriorate (late Lat.), Claud. Mam. de Statu an. 1, 3 al.

la:verb:detrudo.gloss: to expel; dislodge; force, thrust, drive, or shove off, down, or away
senses: to expel; dislodge; force, thrust, drive, or shove off, down, or away
la:verb:detrudo.html:
dē-trūdo, si, sum, 3,
v. a., to thrust, drive, or force away; to thrust down, push down (class.).
Lit.
In gen.: neminem statui detrusum, qui non adhibita vi manu demotus et actus praeceps intellegatur,: qui advorsum eunt, aspellito, Detrude, deturba in viam,: aliquos ad molas,; so, d. et compingere in pistrinum,: in laevam partem oculorum,: quosdam contis remisque in mare,: pedum digitos in terram,: Stygias ad undas,; : sub inania Tartara,: vi tempestatum Cythnum insulam detrusus,: hucine nos ad senem,; cf.: istoc maleficos,: naves scopulo,.—
In partic.
Milit. t. t., to thrust or drive away an enemy from his position; to dislodge, dispossess, ; : Albani prensare, detrudere,i. e. from their horses,; cf.: aliquoties detrusus (sc. de rostris),; ; cf. —
Transf.: ex qua (arce) me nives, frigora, imbres detruserunt, Vatin. ap. —
Jurid. t. t., to drive out a person from his possession, to dispossess (cf. deduco, no. I. B., and deicio, no. I. B.): quid ais? potestne detrudi quisquam, qui non attingitur? etc.,: Quintius contra jus de saltu, agroque communi a servis communibus vi detruditur,—
Trop.
In gen., to drive from or to any thing; to bring, reduce to any thing: aliquem de sua sententia,: a primo ordine in secundum detrudi,: ut detrudendi Domitii causa consulatum peterent,of defeating, keeping him out of office,; cf.: ex quanto regno ad quam fortunam,: se ad mendicitatem,; cf.: ad ea quae nostri ingenii non erunt,: ad id, quod facere possit,: ad necessitatem belli civilis,: in tantum luctum et laborem detrusus,; cf.: aliquem in paupertatem,: eloquentiam in paucissimos sensus et angustas sententias,.—
In partic. of time, to put off, postpone: comitia in mensem Martium,; cf. .

la:verb:detineo.gloss: to hold or keep off or back, detain, check
senses: to hold or keep off or back, detain, check
to delay, hinder, lengthen; occupy, engage, stop
la:verb:detineo.html:
dē-tĭnĕo, tĭnŭi, tentum, 2, v. a.
teneo
,
to hold off, keep back, detain.
Lit. (class.): nos de nostro negotio,: aliquem ab aliquo incepto studioque,: aliquem apud villam,: so, aliquem,; ; Lentul. ap. (with demorari), Oud. N. cr.; (opp. concire); ; : me grata compede Myrtale,; et saep.: novissimos proelio,; cf.: Hannibalem quam acerrimo bello,: se miserandis alimentis detinuerat,had supported himself,: naves tempestatibus detinebantur,; cf.: rates voce canora,: iter iratae anguis (cantus),: illum ne discederet,.—
Trop.
In gen. (poet.), to delay, i. e. lengthen: euntem multa loquendo Detinuit sermone diem,; cf. tempus,.—
Esp., to occupy, engage (also class.): in alienis negotiis detineri,; cf. : in contumelia,: in admiratione sui,: manus in lyricis modis,: mentes hominum circa alia, prooem. § 4: animum studiis,: oculos (mea poëmata),; cf. : animos in timore,.—
To hold in the mind, know: veritatem Dei in injustitia,.

la:verb:detorqueo.gloss: to turn or bend aside, off or away, deflect
senses: to turn or bend aside, off or away, deflect
to twist out of shape, distort
to turn or go (in a direction)
la:verb:detorqueo.html:
dē-torquĕo, si, tum (detorsum,
v.infrano. 1. A. 2.), 2, v. a. and n.
Act., to turn or bend aside, to turn off, turn away (class.).
In gen.
Lit.: ponticulum,: cornua (antennarum),: habenas,: lumen ab illā, et saep.—Poet.: vulnus,.—
With in or ad and acc., to turn in any direction, to direct towards: (orbis partem) a latere in dextram partem,; so, caudam in dexterum, in laevum,: proram ad undas,: cursus ad regem,: cervicem ad oscula, et saep.—
Trop.: voluptates animos a virtute,: quae (sc. voluntas testium) nullo negotio flecti ac detorqueri potest,; .—Of etymolog. derivation: Marrucini vocantur, de Marso detorsum nomen, Cato ap. P.; so, parce detorta,.—With indication of the term. ad quem: aliquem ad segnitiem luxumque,: vividum animum in alia,; cf.: te pravum alio (i. e. ad aliud vitium),.—
In partic., to turn or twist out of shape, to distort.
Lit.: partes corporis detortae,: Vatinius corpore detorto,.—
Trop., to distort, misrepresent: calumniando omnia detorquendoque suspecta efficere,; cf.: recte facta (with carpere),: sincera rectaque ingenia,; cf. : verbum aliquod in pejus,; cf.: verba, voltus in crimen,: sermonem in obscenum intellectum,.— *
Neutr., to turn or go in any direction: in laevam,.
la:verb:detorqueo.inflection: si, tum, 2, v. a. and n.

la:verb:deturbo.gloss: to upset or topple, throw or beat down
senses: to upset or topple, throw or beat down
la:verb:deturbo.html:
dē-turbo, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to drive, thrust, or cast down, to throw or beat down, sc. in a violent, tumultuous manner (freq. and class.; orig. perh. peculiar to milit. lang.).
Lit.: aliquem de pugnaculis,: nostros de vallo lapidibus,; cf.: aliquem ex vallo,: Macedones ex praesidiis stationibusque,; and so in a milit. sense with the simple acc., ; ; ; and absol., : de tecto tegulas,: Trebonium de tribunali,; cf.: aliquem certa re et possessione,: fucos a sedibus suis, et saep.: statuam,; ; cf. aedificium, to pull or tear down, et saep.: Phaëthonta equis in terram,; cf.: praecipitem ab alta puppi in mare,: aliquem in viam,; : caput orantis terrae, to strike to the ground, i. e. to cut off, .—
Trop. (repeatedly in Cic.; elsewhere rare): aliquem de sanitate ac mente,to deprive of,: aliquem ex magna spe,: de fortunis omnibus P. Quinctius deturbandus est,: haec verecundiam mi et virtutis modum deturbavit,.— With abl. alone: neque solum spe, sed certa re jam et possessione deturbatus est,; .

la:verb:detraho.gloss: to draw, pull, take or drag off, down or away; remove, detach, withdraw
senses: to draw, pull, take or drag off, down or away; remove, detach, withdraw
to take away, deprive, diminish, strip, rob
to pull down, drag down, lower
to withdraw, take away, remove; lower in estimation, disparage, detract from
la:verb:detraho.html:
dē-trăho, xi, ctum, 3 (
inf. perf. sync. detraxe, ), v. a., to draw or take off, draw away, draw or take down; to pull down; to take away, remove, withdraw (class. and very freq.).
Lit.
In gen.
With acc. and de or ex with abl.: crumenam sibi de collo,: anulum de digito,: aliquem de curru, et saep.: aliquem ex cruce,; so, stramenta e mulis,: homines ex provinciis,; cf.: inimicum ex Gallia,: Hannibalem ex Italia,; aliquem pedibus e tribunali, et saep.—
With acc. and dat.: nudo vestimenta detrahere me jubes,: alicui anulum,: vestem alicui,: amiculum alicui,: torquem alicui,: loricam alicui, et saep.: tegumenta scutis, : frenos equis, et saep.: virum equo,; cf.: aliquem in transvehendo,.
With acc. alone: vestimenta, Cato ap. : veste detracta,: soccos detrahunt (servi),: detractis insignibus imperatoris,: vestem,; statuas,.—
With ad, in, or trans: castella trans Euphraten, et saep.: aliquem in judicium,; cf.: aliquem ad accusationem,: aliquem ad aequum certamen,: tauros ad terram cornibus,; cf.: naves ad terram, Auct. B. Alex. 10 fin.: dominationem in carcerem et catenas,.—
In partic.
In medic. lang., to purge, ; et saep.—
With the accessory idea of depriving or diminishing, to remove, withdraw, take away a thing from any one; to draw off, remove, take away from any thing.
With acc. and de or ex with abl.: multa de suis commodis,: aliquid de summa,; cf. : aliquid ex ea summa,; and: nihil de vivo,: ex tertia acie singulas cohortes,; cf.: detractis cohortibus duabus,.—
With acc. and dat.: cum ei eidem detraxisset Armeniam,: scuto militi detracto,: coronam capiti,; cf. : auxilia illi,: fasces indigno (opp. deferre), et saep.: pellem hostiae,to flay,.—
With acc. and ab with abl.: aliquid ab homine,.—
Trop.
In gen., to pull down, to lower (very rarely): regum majestatem ab summo fastigio ad medium,: superbiam,.—Far more freq.,
In partic. (acc. to no. I. B. 2.), to withdraw, take away, take; to lower in estimation, disparage, detract from.
With de or ex: detractis de homine sensibus,; cf.: quicquam de nostra benevolentia,: tantum sibi de facultate,; cf.: studiose de absentibus detrahendi causa, severe dicitur,: de ipso, qui scripsit, detrahi nihil volo,: aliquid de aliquo, Caecin. ap. : de hoc senatu detrahere,; so, de aliquo,; : de se,; cf.: de rebus gestis alicujus,: quantum detraxit ex studio, tantum amisit ex gloria,; cf. ; , a.—
With dat.: nihil tibi detraxit senatus nisi, etc. (opp. dare),, b; cf. opp. concedere,; : honorem debitum ordini,: illam opinionem maerenti,: auctoritatem Cottae,: fidem sibi,; : errorem animis,: multum alicui,: regi,.—
Absol.: aliquid dicere detrahendae spoliandaeque dignitatis alicujus gratia, et saep.: laudis simulatione detrahitur,; .—
To withhold: ususfructus in mancipanda proprietate detrahi potest,.

la:verb:detego.html:
dē-tĕgo, xi, ctum, 3,
v. a., to uncover, expose, lay bare (freq. in the Aug. per.).
Lit.: ventus detexit villam,unroofed,: aedem Junonis ad partem dimidiam,: regiam Caci,: juga montium detexerat nebula, et saep.: capite detecto,; cf. poet. transf. and in Gr. construction: caput puer detectus,: faciem,: corpora,: ossa,; et saep.: ensem strictum vagina,; cf. ferrum,: arma,: plagam (opp. celare), et saep.: patefacta et detecta corpora, *.—
In comic transf., to take off, remove: detegetur corium de tergo meo,: haec illa est tempestas mea, mihi quae modestiam omnem Detexit, tectus qua fui (the figure being taken from buildings),; cf. .—
Trop., to discover, disclose, reveal, betray, detect: nimis detegendo cladem nudandoque,: insidias,: consilium,: mentem, prooem. § 20: animi secreta (with proferre mores),: latentem culpam, et saep.: mores se inter ludendum,: formidine detegi,.

la:verb:detono.html:
dē-tŏno, ŭi, 1, v. n.
To thunder down, to thunder.
Prop.: hic (sc. Juppiter) ubi detonuit,.—
Trop., to thunder forth, express in thundertones, to storm (freq. in Florus): captis superioribus jugis in subjectos detonuit,; of Hannibal's invasion of Italy,: adversus epistolam meam turba patricia detonabit,: haec ubi detonuit,; of lofty poetry,.—
To cease thundering; so only trop., to cease raging: Aeneas nubem belli, dum detonet omnis, sustinet, * (bellantum impetum sustinet, donec deferveat, Serv.): ira,: dicendi vitiosa jactatio,.

la:verb:deterrendus.gloss: which is to be deterred or discouraged
senses: which is to be deterred or discouraged

la:adj:detestabilis.html:
dētestābĭlis, e, adj.
detestor
,
execrable, abominable, detestable (good prose): omen,; cf.: exsecratus populo Romano, detestabilis, etc.,fin.: nihil esse tam detestabile tamque pestiferum quam voluptatem,; cf. res (with tetra, misera),: scelus,: exemplum,: voce, et saep.—Comp., ; .—Sup. appears not to occur.—Adv., dētestābĭlĭter, abominably: quod nefarie, quod detestabiliter fecit,.

la:verb:determino.html:
dē-termĭno, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to enclose within boundaries, to bound; to limit, prescribe, determine (rare but class.).
Prop.: regiones, limites, confinia,: augur regiones ab oriente ad occasum determinavit,; cf. Asiam ab oriente Armenia minore, ab occidente Phrygia, etc.,: imaginem templi scipione in solo,.—
Transf., to fix, settle, determine: teli ictus,: segetes in diem,; cf.: diem jejuniis,: senatoria et equestria officia biennio spatio,; : id quod dicit spiritu, non arte determinat,measures,: judicium determinat causas,: mensuram (Ponti),.—Poet.: omnia fixa tuus glomerans determinat annus,.

la:noun:detestatio.html:
dētestātĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
.
In relig. lang.
Execration, cursing, detestation, ; ; ; ; . —
A keeping off, averting, : scelerum,.—
In judicial lang., a formal renunciation under oath: detestatio est denuntiatio facta cum testatione,; cf. detestor, no. II.—So detestatio sacrorum, the solemn renunciation of the family sacred rites, and thereby of the gens itself, which in arrogatio was made by the son, ; cf.: Liber (Servii Sulpicii) de sacris detestandis,.

la:noun:detractor.html:
dētractor, ōris, m.
detraho, no. II. B.
,
a disparager, detractor: sui, (for which, detrectator laudum suarum, ): abominatio hominum detractor,

la:verb:detrahendus.gloss: which is to be removed, detached or withdrawn
senses: which is to be removed, detached or withdrawn

la:noun:determinatio.html:
dētermĭnātĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
,
a boundary, conclusion, end: extrema ora et d. mundi, : exitus et determinatio orationis,.

la:verb:detrunco.html:
dē-trunco, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to lop or cut off (rare, and perh. not ante-Aug.).
Prop.: arbores,: superiorem partem,: alam regi apium,: caput, —
Transf. to the body from which a member is cut off, to mutilate, maim, behead: gladio detruncata corpora bracchiis abscisis,: aliquem,; cf.: Dalmatas incensa urbe quasi detruncaverat,.

la:verb:detexo.html:
dē-texo, xŭi, xtum, 3,
v. a., to weave off, to finish or make by weaving, to weave, plait (mostly poet.).
Lit.: inter decem

annos unam togam, Titin. ap. ; cf.: ad detexundam telam,: vestimentum,.— Comic.: pallium (qs. to take it from the loom),to steal,: aliquid viminibus mollique junco,; cf.: fiscellam vimine junci,.—

Trop., to explain, describe, complete, finish: (lacteus) non perpetuum detexens conficit orbem,: te ab summo jam detexam exordio, Poët. ap. ; cf.: ante exorsa et potius detexta prope retexantur,: at modo coeptum detexatur opus,.

la:verb:deturpo.html:
dē-turpo, āre,
v. a., to disfigure (postAug. and very rare): comatos occipitio raso,: poma rugis. : caput suum, sq.

la:verb:detendo.html:
dē-tendo, no
perf., sum, 3, v. a., to unstretch, relax a thing strained (very rare): tabernacula, to strike the tents, * ; .

la:adj:detrimentosus.html:
dētrīmentōsus, a, um, adj.
detrimentum
,
hurtful, detrimental: ab hoste discedere detrimentosum esse existimabat,.

la:verb:detestamini.gloss: second-person plural present active indicative/imperative of dētestor
senses: second-person plural present active indicative/imperative of dētestor
